title: Introduction to functions
recap: A function gives a name to a focused sequence of statements. Calling that name temporarily transfers execution into the function, and execution resumes immediately after the call when the function finishes.

Small functions make execution order visible and let one tested operation be reused. At this stage, place a function definition before any code that calls it, and keep every named function at file scope rather than inside another function.
objectives: Define a user-written function with a return type, name, parentheses, and body.
Call a function and trace control from caller to callee and back.
Call the same function more than once when an operation must be repeated.
Compose behavior by having one function call other functions.
warnings: Writing a function name without call parentheses does not invoke it.
A function called before its definition is not known to the compiler yet in this lesson.
C++ does not permit a named function definition inside another function.
challenge: Complete the four functions in this order. 1. In checkFlashing(), use std::cout to write exactly `Flashing secure` followed by a newline. 2. In checkVent(), use std::cout to write exactly `Vent clear` followed by a newline. 3. In inspectRoof(), write exactly `Roof inspection started` and a newline, call checkFlashing(), call checkVent(), then write exactly `Roof inspection complete` and a newline. 4. In main(), keep the sequence that writes `Crew dispatched`, calls inspectRoof(), writes `Crew returned`, and returns 0. Keep all three void function definitions above main(), keep their signatures unchanged, qualify cout with std::, and do not add `using namespace std;`.
hints: First complete checkFlashing(): find its TODO and make that function write its one exact result line with std::cout and a newline.

Language-neutral pseudocode: CHECK_FLASHING: OUTPUT `Flashing secure`; CHECK_VENT: OUTPUT `Vent clear`; INSPECT_ROOF: OUTPUT `Roof inspection started`, CALL CHECK_FLASHING, CALL CHECK_VENT, OUTPUT `Roof inspection complete`; MAIN: OUTPUT `Crew dispatched`, CALL INSPECT_ROOF, OUTPUT `Crew returned`, RETURN success.

Near-C++ structure: `void checkFlashing() { <write its required line> }`, `void checkVent() { <write its required line> }`, and `void inspectRoof() { <write start>; checkFlashing(); checkVent(); <write completion>; }`. Keep the existing `int main()` structure and use `std::cout` for each write.
